items.title: Private slave trade in the Dutch Indian Ocean world: a study into the networks and backgrounds of the slavers and the enslaved in South Asia and South Africa
items.who: L. Mbeki and M. van Rossum
items.note: Uses two sets of VOC records on the Cape and Cochin to show officials, soldiers, free citizens and Asians trading slaves privately, outside company accounts.

items.title: Mozambique Island, Cape Town and the Organisation of the Slave Trade in the South-West Indian Ocean, c.1797–1807
items.note: Reconstructs the Mozambique-to-Cape trade under the first British occupation, tracing ships, merchants and routes linking the Indian Ocean and Atlantic trades.

items.title: Dynamics of Indian Ocean Slavery Revealed through Isotopic Data from the Colonial Era Cobern Street Burial Site, Cape Town, South Africa (1750-1827)
items.who: L. M. Kootker, L. Mbeki, A. G. Morris et al.
items.note: Strontium, carbon and nitrogen isotopes identify first-generation forced migrants among the Cape Town burials, an independent check on documented origins.

items.title: Slave Trade Profiteers in the Western Indian Ocean: Suppression and Resistance in the Nineteenth Century
items.note: Studies the merchants and networks that kept the western Indian Ocean trade running under British suppression, using Omani, British and French records.

items.title: Ending the history of silence: reconstructing European slave trading in the Indian Ocean
items.note: Restates and defends Allen's European-carrier estimates, laying out the sources and the gaps that keep the all-carrier total out of reach.

items.title: The Genetic Legacy of the Indian Ocean Slave Trade: Recent Admixture and Post-admixture Selection in the Makranis of Pakistan
items.note: Detects recent Bantu-related African admixture in the Makrani population of Pakistan, attributing it to the Indian Ocean slave trade to the Makran coast.

items.title: Exploring Slave Trade in Asia (ESTA): NWO Internationalisation in the Humanities grant
items.who: M. van Rossum, U. Bosma and F. Ribeiro da Silva (IISH)
items.note: Dutch Research Council grant that funded the first phase of the ESTA voyage database for the Indian Ocean and maritime Asia slave trades.

items.title: Africa and the Indian Ocean World from Early Times to Circa 1900
items.note: Long-run synthesis placing East African and Malagasy slave exports within Indian Ocean economic and environmental cycles.

items.title: Towards an Indian Ocean and Maritime Asia Slave Trade Database: An Exploration of Concepts, Lessons and Models
items.who: S. Sint Nicolaas, M. van Rossum and U. Bosma
items.note: Argues the Atlantic voyage model fits poorly and proposes a data model with voyages, subvoyages and small transfers for Indian Ocean and Asian trades.

items.title: Being a Slave: Histories and Legacies of European Slavery in the Indian Ocean
items.note: Open-access volume of case studies on Dutch and British slavery in Sri Lanka, the Cape and the archipelago, including small-scale Ceylon–Cape trading.

items.title: Towards a global perspective on early modern slave trade: prices of the enslaved in the Indian Ocean, Indonesian Archipelago and Atlantic worlds
items.note: Compiles slave price series across Asian and Atlantic markets, giving a basis for linking local trades and testing demand-side volume estimates.

items.title: VOC Slave Trading Strategies on the Madagascar to Cape Slave Route, 1676-1781
items.note: Examines VOC company voyages from the Cape to Madagascar and the trading strategies behind them, from ship journals and Cape records.

items.title: Abolition and the Registration of Slaves and Libertos in Portuguese Mozambique, 1856–76
items.who: D. B. Domingues da Silva and E. A. Alpers
items.note: Analyses Mozambican slave registers to describe the enslaved population, its origins and its transition to liberto status under Portuguese abolition.

items.title: GLOBALISE: Enriching the VOC Archives
items.note: Machine transcription of the VOC Overgekomen Brieven en Papieren makes scattered slave purchases and transports in company letters full-text searchable.

items.title: NEH grant to add Indian Ocean and maritime Asia voyages to SlaveVoyages
items.who: D. B. Domingues da Silva, R. B. Allen, M. S. Hopper, J. Hooper
items.venue: National Endowment for the Humanities / Rice University
items.note: Three-year project to build an Indian Ocean and Asia voyage database for 1500–1940 within SlaveVoyages, pooling the investigators' existing voyage datasets.

items.title: Exploring Slave Trade in Asia
items.who: P. Konings, M. Hids, S. J. Miske and M. van Rossum
items.note: Describes the ESTA database design, sources and coverage, and the voyage and subvoyage units used to record small and mixed-cargo transports.

items.title: Exploring Slave Trade in Asia (ESTA) Database: first public release
items.note: First open record-level database of slave voyages across the Indian Ocean, archipelago and East Asian seas, launched with about 4,000 voyages and a map viewer.

items.title: Is the SlaveVoyages database useful for scholars of slave trading in the wider Indian Ocean World?
items.note: Compares Atlantic and Indian Ocean evidence and argues that non-African captives were probably the majority of Indian Ocean World traffic.

items.title: The Indian Ocean slave trade and colonial expansion resulted in strong sex-biased admixture in South Africa
items.note: Genetic data from over 1,400 people trace South Asian, Indonesian and East African ancestry from the Cape slave trade and its sex-biased pattern.

items.title: ESTA Database second data launch and TIDES data-entry system
items.note: Expands ESTA to about 5,300 voyages and 9,155 subvoyages referring to at least 440,000 enslaved people, adding China, Mascarene, Mozambique and East India datasets.

items.title: Shifting the Tide: Data, Findings and Future of the Exploring Slave Trade in Asia Database
items.who: P. Konings, M. Tosun and M. van Rossum
items.venue: Colonial Encounters and Slavery in Early Modern Asia (Leiden University Press)
items.note: Reports what the expanded ESTA data show about routes and volumes and what coverage gaps remain.

items.title: Slave Trade in the Indian Ocean: Expanding the SlaveVoyages Database
items.who: D. B. Domingues da Silva and J. Hooper
items.note: Presents preliminary findings of the NEH-funded effort to extend SlaveVoyages to the Indian Ocean and maritime Asia.

items.title: '[We] Cannot Exist Properly without Slaves': New Insights into Early Dutch Slave Trade in Asia from the ESTA Database, 1621–1660
items.who: B. van Duijvenvoorde and P. Konings
items.note: Uses the expanded 2025 ESTA corpus to trace early VOC slave shipments, finding high volumes in the 1620s, a contraction in the 1630s and renewed growth after 1640.

items.title: 'As Many People with the Ships as can be Gotten': Revisiting Enslavement and the Slave Trade on the Coromandel Coast
items.note: Uses VOC archives on Arakan, Bengal and Coromandel to argue that company-linked violent slaving, not famine cycles alone, drove seventeenth-century exports.
